summary: Northwest Florida Beaches International Airport (ECP) opened in 2010 as the first new commercial airport built in the U.S. after the September 11 attacks, replacing the older Panama City–Bay County airport. It sits about 18 miles northwest of Panama City and roughly 20–30 minutes from Panama City Beach, with a modern single terminal and nonstop service from major U.S. carriers. Its name reflects its role as the gateway to the Emerald Coast beaches, St. Andrews State Park, and the Panama City area.
faqs:
Q: How far is ECP from Panama City Beach?
A: It is about 18–20 miles northwest of Panama City Beach, typically a 20–30 minute drive depending on traffic and your specific beach location.

Q: Which airlines serve Northwest Florida Beaches International Airport?
A: Major carriers include American, Delta, Southwest, United, and Allegiant, with nonstop flights to cities such as Atlanta, Dallas/Fort Worth, Nashville, Houston, and Baltimore/Washington. Seasonal routes vary.

Q: What ground transportation is available at ECP?
A: Rental cars, taxis, rideshares, and hotel/private shuttles operate from the terminal area; rental car counters are available at the airport, but advance reservations are recommended in peak season.

Q: Is there parking at the airport?
A: Yes, ECP has short-term and long-term parking lots within walking distance of the terminal, plus a cell phone lot for pickups.
transport_tips: ECP is not on the beach; most travelers rent a car or use rideshare/taxi for the 20–30 minute drive to Panama City Beach. Rental cars are available at the airport, but book early for summer and spring break. If you're being picked up, use the cell phone lot and have your driver wait for a call to avoid circling the terminal.
local_tip: Frequent visitors know that Saturday and Sunday afternoons in summer can bring long baggage claim and rental car lines, so a morning arrival or carry-on-only travel can save significant time.
